name: Bhadarvi Poonam Mela
approximate_date: September (Bhadarvi Poonam full moon, typically early September)
description: A major pilgrimage fair at Ambaji temple, one of the 51 Shakti Peethas, attracting hundreds of thousands of devotees during the full moon of Bhadrapad month. The fair features devotional rituals, folk music, Garba performances, and in recent years, grand drone light shows.
significance: Sacred Shakti Peeth pilgrimage; harvest moon spiritual celebration

name: Janmashtami Festival
description: Ranchhodrai temple in Dakor celebrates Lord Krishna's birthday with elaborate rituals, special prayers, colorful decorations, and traditional dances depicting scenes from Krishna's life. Thousands of devotees gather for special darshan.
significance: Lord Krishna birth anniversary; divine incarnation celebration

name: Sharad Purnima Festival
approximate_date: October (Sharad Purnima full moon, typically mid-October)
description: Celebrated as the day when Lord Krishna appears as Ranchodrai at Dakor temple. Elaborate processions with temple idols, cultural performances, and rituals commemorate the divine love of Radha and Krishna. Thousands of pilgrims gather for special celebrations.
significance: Radha-Krishna divine love celebration; autumn full moon festival

name: Bhavnath Mela (Girnar Mahashivratri Mela)
description: A five-day sacred fair at the Bhavnath Mahadev temple at the foothills of Girnar mountain, honoring Lord Shiva. The fair is renowned for processions of naga sadhus, ritual bathing in holy Mrugi Kund, devotional singing through the night, and traditional bhavai folk dances. Attracts thousands of pilgrims and ascetics.
significance: Lord Shiva veneration; major pilgrimage and ashram gathering

name: Uttarardh Mahotsav (Modhera Dance Festival)
description: A two-day classical dance festival celebrating the winter solstice at the ancient Sun Temple. The festival showcases diverse Indian classical dance forms including Odissi, Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Manipuri, Kuchipudi, Kathakali, and Sattriya. Named after the astronomical halfway point of the sun's northward journey, honoring the sun god.
significance: Celebration of classical arts and solar astronomy

name: Mandvi Beach Festival
description: A ten-day coastal cultural festival at Mandvi Beach with free entry, featuring nightly cultural musical performances with renowned artists on weekends. The festival includes adventure activities, beach sports, sand art, bonfire arrangements, live music, stargazing sessions, laser light shows, and traditional craft and food stalls against the Arabian Sea backdrop.
significance: Coastal cultural celebration; year-end festive gathering

name: Dholavira Festival
approximate_date: Varies (cultural heritage festival, dates to be announced)
description: A heritage festival blending archaeology with contemporary performance at India's oldest urban site. Features interactive heritage walks through the Harappan city layout, traditional crafts demonstrations including block printing and bead making, and performances by folk and classical musicians. Free entry for all visitors, promoting heritage-based tourism and archaeological education.
significance: Archaeological heritage celebration; Harappan civilization education

name: Navratri Festival (Dandiya & Garba)
description: Major celebration across Bhavnagar city featuring traditional Dandiya and Garba dance performances during the nine-day festival of Navratri. Young generations gather to celebrate the victory of good over evil with traditional dances, prayers, and festive gatherings.
significance: Divine feminine worship; seasonal harvest celebration
